title: schema2object
description: JSON Schema IS the object class. ObjectTree IS the runtime instance. Construction IS validation.

exports.description: Three exports. Each has ONE job. Do not mix.

ObjectTree.description: Runtime instance — schema-bound object with validated property access. Construction = validation. Who uses it, who builds it.

static.description: Static class fields — shared across all instances.

_observer.description: Global observer hook. fn(op, path, key, val, schema) or null. Schema context added in v0.5.2.
_observer.x-signature: (op: 'get'|'set', path: string, key: string, val: any, schema?: object) => void | null

x-behavior.enabled: Called on every get/set, schema parameter provides schema node for property

constructor.description: new ObjectTree(data, schema, resolver) — validates data, builds runtime, fills defaults. One step.

description.const: Initial data. Validated against schema on construction.
JSON Schema Draft-07 object. Can contain $ref — resolved via resolver.
Schema file path — dirname becomes base dir for $ref resolution
URI-to-schema map — keys are URIs, values are schema objects

behavior.description: What happens on new ObjectTree(data, schema, resolver)

step1.const: Build Loader from resolver (or reuse if Loader instance)

step3.const: Validate data against schema (throws on invalid)

step4.const: Fill defaults for missing keys only — validate each default, throw if invalid

step5.const: Wrap in Proxy cursor — raw data stored as-is, nested access is lazy

fields.description: Internal state via Symbols. Property access intercepted by Proxy — no upfront defineProperty.

_RAW.description: Raw data — plain object from JSON.parse, not copied

_CACHE.description: Map of key → child ObjectTree (lazy, populated on first access)

methods.description: All API methods use $ prefix. Data properties don't. Zero collision.

$value.description: Get/set raw data. Getter returns raw object directly. Setter validates then overwrites.

get.const: Returns raw data — plain object or scalar, no unwrapping needed

set.const: Validates against schema then overwrites raw data, clears cache

$oneOf.description: XOR dispatch — exactly one oneOf branch must match. Returns new ObjectTree bound to matching branch schema.

$anyOf.description: OR dispatch — all matching anyOf branches. Returns array of ObjectTree.

$allOf.description: AND merge — deep-merge all allOf sub-schemas. Returns new ObjectTree.

$notOf.description: Negation check — returns boolean. true if data does NOT match 'not' schema.

$ifThen.description: Conditional — if data matches 'if' schema, bind to 'then'; else bind to 'else'. Returns ObjectTree.

$project.description: SELECT — keep only schema-defined properties. Returns new ObjectTree.

$withDefaults.description: Fill missing defaults from schema. Returns new ObjectTree.

$contains.description: Array element match — returns boolean. true if any item matches 'contains' schema.

$toDict.description: Terminal operation — serialize to plain object. Schema-defined fields only. ONE-WAY EXIT. Do not manipulate result.
$toDict.x-anti-pattern: const d = tree.$toDict(); d.name = 'x' — loses schema binding

$schema.description: Getter — returns deep copy of resolved schema as plain object.

$getSchema.description: $getSchema('address.city') — navigate to sub-schema by dot path.

$getExtensions.description: $getExtensions() — returns all x-* extension fields from schema.

toJSON.description: JS protocol — called by JSON.stringify(). Delegates to $toDict().

correct: user.$oneOf().role — chain methods, stay in ObjectTree
wrong: const d = user.$toDict(); d.name = 'x' — detached from schema
const {name} = user — destructuring loses schema binding
new ObjectTree(data, schema); // discard — construction is not free

Loader.description: Resolves $ref per JSON Schema Draft-07 URI semantics. One Loader per schema document root.

description.const: Root schema object — $ref '#' resolves to this
Base URI for relative $ref. Falls back to root.$id.

step1.const: Scan all $id in schema tree, build idMap

step2.const: Track scope (base URI) and resource (nearest $id ancestor) per node

resolve.description: resolve(ref, baseUri, resourceUri) — returns {node, loader}. Handles: '#', '#/pointer', '#anchor', relative, absolute, remote.

scopeOf.description: Base URI for relative $ref resolution at this node.

parentScopeOf.description: Base URI ignoring own $id — for sibling $id-ignore rule.

resourceOf.description: Nearest $id-bearing ancestor URI — '#' resolves to this.

forms.#/path: JSON Pointer within nearest resource root
forms.relative: Resolved against base URI, then loaded

remote-loading.string-resolver: Directory path — URI path mapped to filesystem

validate.description: Gate check — pass/fail only. Uses new ObjectTree() internally (same validation logic, no duplication). Returns {valid, error?}.

x-usage.correct: Gate check at boundary — reject invalid before proceeding
x-usage.wrong: validate() then operate on raw dict — why validate if you won't use ObjectTree?

ThreeRoles.description: Three exports, three roles. Do not mix.

ObjectTree.const: Runtime instance — live with it, operate on it

validate.const: Bouncer — checks the ticket, does not enter the venue

$toDict.const: Exit door — one-way, do not re-enter

CorrectFlow.description: Input boundary → validate. Business logic → ObjectTree. Output boundary → $toDict.

step2_runtime.const: tree = new ObjectTree(data, schema) — property access, chain methods

step3_output.const: tree.$toDict() / JSON.stringify(tree) — serialize once, send out
